title: Development and validation of an AI foundation model for endoscopic diagnosis of esophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma: a cohort and deep learning study.
summary: Multicentre study of esophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma staging: 12,302 images/1,546 patients from seven hospitals; DINOv2 and ResNet50 encoders are gated in a mixture-of-experts classifier. Pathology is the reference; patient-disjoint held-out, external, and prospective cohorts plus an endoscopist reader comparison support a bounded diagnostic finding. It does not establish broader clinical benefit; data are from seven Chinese hospitals and image-level training is discussed. The arXiv v1 is the first located result-bearing version; its prospective accuracy was 0.8956, compared with 0.8963 in the later journal version.
ai_technology: DINOv2 extracts global appearance and ResNet50 local detail; element-wise gating/MoE fuses representations before three-class classification.
organization: Shanghai Research Institute for Intelligent Autonomous Systems

evidence.tested: Results at image and patient levels report accuracy/AUC across held-out, external and prospective sets and comparison with endoscopists.
evidence.unknown: Histopathology defines early/advanced disease; held-out 112-patient, external 230-patient and prospective 198-patient sets; human reader comparisons. Regional sampling and image-level training limit generalizability; no patient outcome tested.
evidence.ai_role: DINOv2 extracts global appearance and ResNet50 local detail; element-wise gating/MoE fuses representations before three-class classification.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
